citations.narrative:
The facility is still not adequately cleaning the enclosure for seven Egyptian fruit bats. The wooden surfaces inside the
enclosure are coated in a mottled brown material and old food debris, especially below areas where the bats hang from
the ceiling. The inspector also saw numerous live roaches below one of the dirty wooden structures. The facility
representative stated that they were planning to move the bats into a new enclosure soon; however, the current enclosure
housing the bats is not being cleaned as often as necessary.
Inadequate cleaning can result in an accumulation of excreta and other waste in the enclosure, which can increase the
likelihood of disease hazards and attract pests. Excreta shall be removed from primary enclosures as often as necessary
to prevent contamination of the animals contained therein and to minimize disease hazards and to reduce odors.

The facility still does not have adequate pest control for roaches. The inspector saw numerous live roaches inside the
enclosure housing seven Egyptian fruit bats.
Pests such as roaches can spread disease and contaminate food, surfaces, and animal housing areas. A safe and
effective program for the control of insects, ectoparasites, and avian and mammalian pests shall be established and
maintained.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
